name: Evergreen Park
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Evergreen Park, IL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Evergreen Park, IL: Breakfast with Santa at the American Legion, the free Sounds of the Season concert and Santa house calls.
lede: Evergreen Park starts the season at Klein Park with Santa's Wonderland and the Reindog Parade, then lights the village tree. December also brings Santa to the library, a Santa breakfast at the American Legion and a free orchestra concert at Most Holy Redeemer Church.
celebrates: Christmas in Evergreen Park centers on Klein Park, the star-shaped circle on 97th Street where eight streets meet. Each December the Recreation Department hosts Santa's Wonderland and the Reindog Parade there, with dogs in holiday outfits, a visit from Santa, food, music and the annual tree lighting. Santa also makes house calls: residents can book a home visit through the Recreation Department, and Santa works for tips. The Evergreen Park Public Library hosts Santa Saturday with Dreezy Claus, American Legion Post 854 serves Breakfast with Santa, and the season winds down with the free Sounds of the Season concert by the City Lights Orchestra at Most Holy Redeemer Church.
lastyear: In 2025, Santa's Wonderland and the Reindog Parade was planned for Saturday, December 13, at Klein Park. With cold temperatures in the forecast, the village moved many activities indoors. The Reindog Parade stayed outside at 1:30 pm, while the vendor fair, Santa visits, cookie decorating, Disney character visits, food vendors and a DJ moved inside, and a brief tree lighting was set for 5 pm. The Sounds of the Season concert was planned for December 21 at Most Holy Redeemer Church, and Dreezy Claus was scheduled to visit the library the weekend before Christmas.
facts: Evergreen Park was incorporated on December 20, 1893, after 41 of 50 residents voted to stay separate from Chicago. A developer inspired by the Arc de Triomphe in Paris designed a star-shaped park with eight streets running out from it, and the evergreen trees planted there gave the village its name. After Mayor Henry Klein died, shortly after the village's 75th anniversary in 1968, the park was renamed Klein Park. With thirteen congregations close together, Evergreen Park is also called the Village of Churches.
trains: Trains are part of Evergreen Park's story. The first line, which later became part of the Grand Trunk Railroad, passed through in 1873, and when St. Mary's Cemetery opened in 1888, mourners rode the train from Chicago. In July 1918 a spark from a passing train set the first village hall on fire. Today Pace and CTA buses serve the village. For train fun, the Griffin Museum of Science and Industry in Chicago runs The Great Train Story, a 3,500-square-foot model railroad, and the Illinois Railway Museum in Union is the largest railway museum in the US.

kidfact: Evergreen Park's birthday is December 20, 1893, so the village turns a year older just before Christmas. Its name comes from the evergreen trees planted in the park that is now Klein Park.
faq: Where is the Evergreen Park tree lighting?

The village lights its tree at Klein Park, the circle park by the Community Center at 3450 W. 97th Street. The Tree Lighting Ceremony comes at the end of Santa's Wonderland and the Reindog Parade, an afternoon the Recreation Department hosts each December with Santa, food, music and family activities before the lights come on.

It is the dog parade that opens Santa's Wonderland. Families dress their dogs in Christmas outfits and walk them around Klein Park. In 2025 there was a prize for the best dressed pet, and pets could have photos taken with Santa. Right after the parade, Santa's Wonderland begins, and the tree lighting caps the day.
Can Santa visit our house in Evergreen Park?

Yes, if you live in the village. The Evergreen Park Recreation Department books Santa for home visits on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays in December, up to Christmas Eve. Santa works for tips, with a $10 minimum per visit. Call the Recreation Department at 708-229-3373 to reserve a time for your family.
How do I get tickets to the Sounds of the Season concert?

Tickets are free but limited. The Recreation Department hands them out first come, first served at the Community Center, 3450 W. 97th Street, starting in November, with up to four per household. The concert features the City Lights Orchestra and Vocalists, conducted by Rich Daniels, at Most Holy Redeemer Church on Lawndale Avenue.
Does Santa visit the Evergreen Park library?

Yes. The Evergreen Park Public Library, 9400 S. Troy Avenue, hosts Santa Saturday in December with holiday activities, snacks and a visit from Dreezy Claus, known as Chicago's Black Santa. Families are asked to register ahead, and the library suggests bringing a camera if you would like a picture with Santa.
